thread.title: Apple: HomePod ‘mini’? Apple Watch at $10B? Guggenheim Dissects ‘Other’

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple: HomePod ‘mini’? Apple Watch at $10B? Guggenheim Dissects ‘Other’
text:
Apple's Apple Watch Series 3. Illustration: Tiernan Ray for Barron's Apple ’s ( AAPL ) sales of everything “Other” — the line item in its quarterlies that consists of Apple Watch , AirPod wireless ear buds, the HomePod speaker systems, etc. — is primed to reach $22 billion in 2019, double the $11 billion it was in 2016, according to a report out this evening from Guggenheim ’s Robert Cihra.
Cihra, who maintains a Buy rating on Apple, and a $215 price target, thinks it will be Apple’s fourth-biggest line of revenue this calendar year, at more than $19 billion, making up 7% of revenue, after iPhone, the services business, and the Mac. It will surpass iPads as a component of revenue.
And of that, he expects Apple Watch alone will make up half of Other, or $9.5 billion, at 22 million units.
The AirPod ear buds may top $3 billion this year, on sales of perhaps 23 million units, as they have been “an upside hit over the past year.” At that rate, they will top the “Beats” headphone brand, he estimates. that’s $13.8 billion in wearable tech sales this year, he writes.
With HomePod, Cihra expects sales of 3 million units this year, or $1 billion in revenue.
He looks forward to a HomePod “mini,” and further capabilities:
Primarily a Siri/Apple Music cloud-access device today, the HomePod nevertheless has a real brain (A8 chip + 16GB NAND) that we see opening up potential for more local edge processing, including on-device ML/AI. A HomePod MINI could follow and we expect its price-point to signal whether Apple ultimately sees smart speakers more as a profit center or defensive Siri/ AI beachhead.
Cihra writes that all this should be taken as Apple’s constellation of devices at the “edge” of the network, rather than in the cloud:
We think of Services leveraging Apple’s CLOUD deliverables (e.g., Apps and media, Siri cloud-based ML/AI) but Accessories at the EDGE, further monetizing Apple’s installed-base and services, able to either build in more on-device ML/AI or provide a direct conduit to the cloud that does not require an iPhone in between.
Apple shares today closed up $3.03, or 1.8%, at $167.37.
